added_models.model: Human platelet-rich plasma in vitro, ADP-induced aggregation (TRK-100/beraprost)

engagement.model: Human platelet-rich plasma in vitro, ADP-induced aggregation (TRK-100/beraprost)
engagement.note: Beraprost (TRK-100) potently inhibited ADP-induced aggregation of human platelet-rich plasma in vitro.
engagement.short: Inhibits human platelet aggregation in vitro
engagement.quote: The drug was shown to be a potent inhibitor of platelet aggregation in vitro, induced by adenosine diphosphate (ADP), using platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from human and several animal species.

engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo ADP aggregation inhibition after 40-60 ug oral doses vs in vitro IC50 (no exposure-matched comparison)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Healthy volunteers; effect was brief (0.5-1 h) and poorly related to plasma APS-314d.
engagement.judgement: Paired by us: the in vitro human platelet readout (ADP aggregation) is the same readout measured ex vivo in dosed humans, so readout_tier direct.
engagement.model: Human platelet-rich plasma in vitro, ADP-induced aggregation (TRK-100/beraprost)
engagement.note: Oral beraprost 40 and 60 ug inhibited ex vivo ADP-induced platelet aggregation in 12 healthy volunteers; 20 ug did not.
engagement.quote: BPS 40 and 60 micrograms decreased platelet aggregation 1 h after single doses, and 0.5 h and 1 h after repeated doses.
engagement.reason: Ex vivo platelet inhibition in volunteers

added_models.model: PAH-patient PASMC proliferation and human distal pulmonary artery myography ex vivo (esuberaprost)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Co-authors include sponsor-side staff (von Kessler, Sista). Published May 2019, after BEAT primary completion (Feb 2019) but before results were posted (Feb 2020).
efficacy.judgement: Esuberaprost (BPS-314d) is the active stereoisomer within racemic beraprost, so it is treated as the member drug beraprost; a stricter reading of the member list would drop this track.
efficacy.model: PAH-patient PASMC proliferation and human distal pulmonary artery myography ex vivo (esuberaprost)
efficacy.note: Esuberaprost, beraprost's 314d isomer, inhibited proliferation of PAH-patient PASMCs (EC50 3 nM) and relaxed patient pulmonary arteries.
efficacy.quote: In human PASMCs, esuberaprost was 40-fold more potent than beraprost at inhibiting cell proliferation (EC50 3 nM versus 120 nM), contrasting the 5-fold potency difference for cAMP elevation.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: clinical worsening events, esuberaprost 49/136 vs placebo 51/135 (added to inhaled treprostinil)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (posted 2020-02-28) give event counts by component (8+23+7+6+5=49 vs 13+14+13+4+7=51) without inference; a 2026 Research Square preprint states 'There was no difference between treatment groups in time to clinical worsening (primary endpoint)'. No peer-reviewed paper found.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: contra although the trial was add-on to another IP agonist (inhaled treprostinil), a condition the ex vivo model never tested; retrodiction false because the trial result was not public when the model paper appeared, though the sponsor may have known topline.
efficacy.model: PAH-patient PASMC proliferation and human distal pulmonary artery myography ex vivo (esuberaprost)
efficacy.note: BEAT: esuberaprost added to inhaled treprostinil did not reduce clinical worsening (49 vs 51 patients) in 271 PAH patients.
efficacy.short: BEAT: no effect on clinical worsening
efficacy.quote: The number of participants that experienced clinical worsening is presented; time to clinical worsening data was not measured.

considered_not_added: Cynomolgus monkey PK for ralinepag (Tran 2017, 'very low peak-to-trough ratio' from enterohepatic recirculation): humans showed QD peak-to-trough 3.3-4.5 and needed BID or an XR tablet (Pulm Circ 2020), but the monkey data stated no human exposure or regimen target, so dose would be untested/no_prediction; not added as a track
Ralinepag and esuberaprost in vitro human IP receptor cAMP assays (Tran 2017; Shen 2019): no readout with a human counterpart

Chronic hypoxia rat with beraprost (+/- sildenafil, AJRCCM 2004, doi:10.1164/rccm.200303-346oc): no patient comparison for beraprost alone beyond what the MCT rat track already pairs; combination never tested in patients
Hamster cheek-pouch thrombosis / 'without the hypotensive activity of PGI2' claim (Sim 1985): antithrombotic, not PAH; the no-hypotension claim was not compared with PAH patient data

Short-term haemodynamic series of oral beraprost in PPH (Saji 1996, doi:10.1016/s0002-9149(96)90408-7) and ralinepag phase 2/ADVANCE OUTCOMES: patient-side data for the existing mct-rat track, not new model systems
In-silico / QSP, human genetic, patient-derived organoid or PDX models for PTGIR agonists in PAH: none found
